findings.motion: HB 958, Election Law Changes, Senate Second Reading (28 ayes, 13 noes); Lazzara is listed among the ayes
findings.note: Senate vote on a multi-part election bill. The ratified text says a county board may process a voter registration application only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship. If the citizenship answer is blank, the applicant gets a notice and must return a citizenship statement under penalty of perjury within 30 days. It also directs the State Board of Elections to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The Governor vetoed the bill on 08/17/2026 (per the bill page). The House vote on the concur motion was on 8/4/2026.
NC Senate, Third Reading (roll call #677), 2024-12-02: yea (tally 30–19); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)

findings.motion: Senate second reading, HB 958 Election Law Changes (RCS S-693, 28 to 13)
findings.note: Voted Aye on second reading in the Senate. Roll call shown on the official bill page. HB 958, Election Law Changes (2025-26 session). Per the official bill digest it, among other things: requires a statement of US citizenship (under penalty of perjury) on voter registration applications; requires covered military and overseas voters to send a copy of the photo ID used for in-person voting with the ballot; and extends the deadline for a voter to show ID after a provisional ballot to noon on the fifth business day after the election. It was ratified 2026-08-06 and vetoed by the Governor 2026-08-17.

Listed as a primary sponsor of S 356 (2023-24 session). The bill was filed as a motor-vehicle-dealer bill; its Edition 3 text, titled Constitutional Amendment/Photo ID, proposes a state constitutional amendment on photographic identification for voters. The page does not show who wrote the Edition 3 change. The bill's last action was referral to a House committee on 2024-06-27.
